To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the α1(I):CAT transgene is activated in a subset of cells within the dermis in response to TGF-β; (2) the α1(1):CAT transgene was activated in the lung in response to bleomycin, but not in a uniform manner
the transgene is expressed in a subpopulation of fibroblasts that respond to TGF‐B and that a subset of fibroblastic cells in lung express the endogenous collagen gene but not the transgene.

the transgene responds to TGF-β in a subset dermal fibroblast, but not in all dermal fibroblaasts and that bleomycin induced lung fibrosis is associated with increased expression of the transgene in the interstitum of the lung, but not in the myofibroblast surrounding airways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms that regulate collagen synthesis in the skin and lung.
the study of the molecular biology of the extracellular matrix (ECM), the complex meshwork of fibrous proteins and glycosaminoglycans that surrounds cells in tissues and organs.
understanding the mechanisms that control gene expression in the skin and lung, and the role of TGF‐beta in fibrosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the α1(I)-CAT transgene is expressed in most connective tissue cells in a tissue specific manner, but not all cells in a given tissue are expressing the transgene.
the transgene expression in lung fibrosis is similar to the expression of endogenous gene in lung fibroblasts but not in myofibroblast.
TGF‐β induces a subset of cells in the dermis to express the CAT gene, but not the α1(I)-collagen gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collagen α1(I)-promoter/CAT transgene can be used to study the response of fibroblasts to TGF‐beta.
TGF‐β is a major mediator of fibroblast‐specific α1(I)collagen gene expression and that the α1(I)cis elements are responsive to other factors in addition to TGF‐B.
we are trying to understand how cells in a particular tissue respond to a stimulus, in this case, TGF‐β, and how that response differs from other tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α1(I)-collagen gene promoter is a good reporter gene for the study of connective tissue gene expression.
the transgene is not a perfect surrogate for the endogenous gene.
there are subsets of fibroblasts that respond to TGF‐beta and express the endogenous gene, but not CAT gene.
